2. CLINICAL RATIONALE & GUIDELINES APPLIED



   Reason for Adverse Determination:

   Your spine surgeon requested prior approval for a 3-day acute care inpatient hospital admission following a
   planned single-level lumbar spine fusion (L4-L5). While single-level lumbar fusion is a covered benefit under your
   Healthfirst Silver Leaf Plan when criteria are met, our medical reviewer determined that an acute care inpatient
   hospital admission is NOT medically necessary.

   Clinical Review Guidelines Used: InterQual® 2026 Acute Adult Guidelines (Spinal Procedures: Lumbar Fusion) &
   Healthfirst Clinical Coverage Policy #SP-019 (Surgical Inpatient vs. Outpatient Observation Criteria).

   Detailed Rationale: Medical records submitted by Dr. Sarah Jenkins on 10/28/2026 were reviewed by a board-
   certified orthopedic physician reviewer. The documentation demonstrates that you are a 58-year-old male
   undergoing a single-level posterior lumbar fusion. The notes do not document significant comorbidities—such
   as severe cardiopulmonary instability, ASA physical status class III/IV, morbid obesity (BMI > 45), or acute
   neurological deficits—that require multi-day acute inpatient nursing care. Guidelines specify that single-level
   lumbar interbody fusions without complex surgical risk factors should be performed in an ambulatory surgical
   setting or managed under short-term observation (under 24–48 hours). Therefore, the request for a 3-day
   inpatient stay is denied.

3. HOW TO APPEAL THIS DECISION (YOUR APPEAL RIGHTS)


If you, your authorized representative, or your doctor disagree with this denial, you have the right to request an
Internal Appeal. During an internal appeal, independent Healthfirst physician specialists will review the clinical
records, guidelines, and any additional medical information you provide.



   Important Filing Deadline: You have 180 calendar days from the date of this letter to request an appeal (Deadline:
   May 2, 2027). Appeal requests filed after this date will not be accepted. There is no fee to submit an appeal.



4. STANDARD VS. EXPEDITED APPEAL PROCEDURES


Standard Internal Appeal:


Healthfirst will send a written determination within 30 calendar days of receiving your appeal. You or your physician
should include supplementary medical records (e.g., physical therapy notes, pain management reports, or physician
statements explaining why outpatient observation is unsafe for your condition).


Expedited (Fast-Track) Appeal:


If waiting 30 days could seriously harm your life, health, or recovery, you or your physician may request an expedited
appeal. Healthfirst will evaluate the request and provide a final verbal and written determination within 72 hours.


5. APPEAL SUBMISSION DETAILS


Submit your appeal request along with any supporting documents to Healthfirst via any of the following methods:


 By Mail:                          Healthfirst Appeals & Grievances Department
                                   P.O. Box 5166, New York, NY 10274-5166

 Online Member Portal:             Submit via member account at my.healthfirst.org


6. NY STATE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES (DFS) EXTERNAL APPEAL


If Healthfirst upholds this denial following an internal appeal, you have the right to request an External Appeal through
the New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS). An independent medical panel appointed by the state
will review your appeal. You must submit your External Appeal application to the NYS DFS within 4 months of
receiving Healthfirst's final appeal determination notice.
